planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Anthurium besseae is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to moderate shade in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, since this species needs adequate light for healthy leaf production but will bleach and scorch in direct sun. Anthurium besseae produces deep green, velvety, heart-shaped leaves marked by bold, contrasting deep red to burgundy veining, especially vivid on new growth before it matures and darkens, giving each unfurling leaf a striking color display distinct from the mostly white or silver venation of many other collector anthuriums. Water thoroughly when the top layer of the chunky mix dries, since the plant is more drought-tolerant than humidity-tolerant and chronic overwatering causes rapid root rot; maintain warm temperatures and high humidity for the best leaf color and growth rate.

common_name: Luxurians Anthurium (Thick Corrugated Dark Green Anthurium)

planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Anthurium luxurians is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to moderate shade in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, since this species needs adequate light for healthy leaf production but will bleach and scorch in direct sun. Anthurium luxurians produces thick, deeply quilted, near-black-green leaves with an intensely corrugated, almost bubbled surface texture that catches light dramatically, one of the most heavily textured leaf surfaces among commonly collected anthurium species. The bold, sculptural leaf texture gives it strong presence as a specimen plant even without considering its aroid inflorescence. Water thoroughly when the top layer of the chunky mix dries, since the plant is more drought-tolerant than humidity-tolerant and chronic overwatering causes rapid root rot; maintain warm temperatures and high humidity for the best growth and leaf texture.

planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Anthurium metallicum is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water. Give it room to grow, since mature leaves become quite large.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to moderate shade in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, since this species needs adequate light for healthy leaf production but will bleach and scorch in direct sun. Anthurium metallicum is among the largest and most dramatic velvet-leaf anthurium species, producing huge, heart-shaped leaves with a distinctive metallic, almost pewter-like sheen over deep green velvet, prominently marked with pale sunken venation. Its substantial mature size and striking metallic luster make it a serious floor specimen for collectors with enough space and consistently warm, humid conditions to support it. Water thoroughly when the top layer of the chunky mix dries, since the plant is more drought-tolerant than humidity-tolerant and chronic overwatering causes rapid root rot.

common_name: Leuconeurum Anthurium (White-Veined Ace of Spades Anthurium)

planting.note: Grow in bright indirect light in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix; Anthurium leuconeurum is particularly susceptible to root rot, so never allow the pot to sit in standing water.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to moderate shade in very well-drained, chunky, perlite-enriched aroid mix, since this species needs adequate light for healthy leaf production but will bleach and scorch in direct sun. Anthurium leuconeurum, sometimes called Ace of Spades for its distinctly pointed, spade-shaped leaf outline, produces deep green, matte to semi-velvety leaves crisply marked with bright white venation that stands out sharply against the dark leaf surface. Its more compact size compared to giant species like metallicum makes it a manageable collector's plant for a smaller bright shelf or grow-light setup. Water thoroughly when the top layer of the chunky mix dries, since the plant is more drought-tolerant than humidity-tolerant and chronic overwatering causes rapid root rot; maintain warm temperatures and high humidity for the best growth.
